reasons: Both answers propose essentially the same hybrid of central policy plus isolated per-channel delivery, with a separate OTP lane, quiet hours for marketing only, and a push-before-SMS cascade. B addresses the rubric's key merge conflict directly: it checks the idempotency key both in the orchestrator and in the SMS worker before the provider call, and it rechecks quiet hours before sending. A covers the quiet-hours recheck and provider-side duplicates but never says where dedup lives across per-channel retries. B also adds concrete cost controls (per-user and daily SMS caps with an 80% alert) and a practical single-codebase deployment with a --role flag, while A has a few more hedges but no substantive advantage.
